text.p: Following are the main stories in today's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysia will announce fiscal measures in the annual budget for 1998, including tax breaks, to boost exports and curb imports, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the Penang international airport would be closed and the island state would be served by a new international airport proposed on a man-made island off northern Kedah state.

-- Shipping firm Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd said it hopes to conclude negotiations to take a 29.35 percent stake in national shipping firm Malaysian International Shipping Corp by end-September. The deal was worth more than two billion ringgit and stuck on disagreements over price.

-- Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the eight percent economic growth target for 1997 was achievable and that the economy was in no fear of overheating. he said the growth rate of eight percent was sustainable for the next 30 years.
